protein: Tgo-D4K (engineered FANA polymerase)
readout: FANA synthesis rate, normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent (fold)
assay_method: Polymerase kinetic profiling (PKPro). 20 nM polymerase, 1 uM 30-mer DNA template, 100 uM each NTP, 1x ThermoPol buffer, 2x LC Green Plus; denature 95 degC 3 min, extend 55 degC 30 min, fluorescence every 6 s; rate from a linear fit of nucleotides per polymerase vs time; mean of three independent replicates.
remark: No WT row: the readout is already normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent, which is 1.0 by definition. The reference sequence is the engineered Tgo-D4K parent, not native Tgo. Position 659 follows the source data, which carries Y and lists the variant as Y659E; the paper text instead calls it H659E. Q93A is listed twice with values differing by 7e-5, and the mean is used.

protein: IFRS (pyrrolysyl-tRNA synthetase MmPylRS N346I/C348S, charges 3-bromo-Phe onto tRNA-Pyl for amber suppression)
readout: Stop codon suppression efficiency, normalized to the IFRS parent (fold)
assay_method: Amber suppression of sfGFP-S2TAG in E. coli co-expressing the PylRS variant (glnS promoter) and PylT (lpp promoter) with 3-bromo-Phe (3BrF). Cells grown to OD600 0.4-0.6, resuspended in minimal medium, induced with 0.2 percent arabinose, 12 h at 37 degC; fluorescence on a BioTek Synergy H1 (ex/em 485/515 nm), background-corrected and divided by OD600; the Flu/OD of cells cultured without ncAA is subtracted, and the result divided by the parent measured alongside. Triplicate in Fig. 1b, 1c, 1e, 1g, 2c, 2f, 2h and Supplementary Fig. 6; a single value in the Fig. 2b and 2d screens and the Fig. 2g test set.
remark: The reference sequence is IFRS, MmPylRS translated from the supplementary DNA (Supplementary Data Table 1) with the paper's own specificity mutations N346I/C348S applied, and otherwise identical to UniProt Q8PWY1. There is no WT row, the parent reading 1.0 by definition rather than by measurement, and each readout is the mean of its panel's replicates after collapsing variants appearing in more than one panel, the worst disagreement being K67R at 0.527 in Fig. 2d against 0.801 in Fig. 2b, where the Fig. 2d value is taken; the wild-type sfGFP control of Fig. 2h and the parent-residue cells of the Fig. 2d landscape are not variants and are dropped. The second engineering round is reported against Com1-IFRS and is rebased onto the IFRS scale by that parent's own value of 11.1247, with every label re-derived from the assembled sequence so that substitutions landing on the seven positions Com1-IFRS already carries compose rather than duplicate, which leaves the two rounds joined at that single genotype and nowhere else; Fig. 2h is converted from normalized fluorescence by the Com1-IFRS mean of that panel and its Z7-n labels expanded through Supplementary Table 8. The paper's text places the counts of mutations improving on Com1-IFRS by more than 10 percent at positions V73 and D75 while the source data columns are V74 and D76, and the stated counts of 2 and 9 reproduce only at V74/D76, so the data numbering is followed. Not extracted from this paper: catalytic efficiency kcat/Km(tRNA), reported for too few variants; the ncAA panel of Fig. 3, which measures separate parent synthetases rather than one wild type; and the myoglobin and multiple-amber constructs of Fig. 4, each carrying two or three variants.

protein: TEVp 0, the engineered tobacco etch virus NIa protease used as the library parent; it carries T17S, L56V, N68D, I77V, S135G and S219V relative to the viral polyprotein
readout: log2 protease activity on the canonical TEVs motif ENLYFQ|S, relative to the TEVp 0 parent
assay_method: DNA recorder in E. coli: a TEVp variant and a barcoded TEVs substrate are co-expressed, cleavage releases a degron-tagged Bxb1 recombinase that permanently inverts a DNA segment, and the inverted fraction is read by NGS of the paired protease and substrate barcodes over a 4 h induction.
remark: The reference sequence is the library parent TEVp 0, the 242-residue NIa protease of UniProt P04517 carrying T17S, L56V, N68D, I77V, S135G and S219V; the paper states no sequence, so the parent residue at each scanned position was read off the site-saturation scan, where the parent's own row reads exactly 0 at all 234 positions, and the result was corroborated against 44 mutation labels printed in full elsewhere in the workbook, which verify without exception. Of the 4446 single substitutions the paper reports as theoretically possible across positions 1-234, 38 carry no measurement and are dropped, and the 234 rows in which the substituted residue equals the parent residue are the parent itself rather than variants, so they collapse into the single WT row. Residues 235-242 are outside the scanned range and rest on the reference sequence alone. Not extracted from this paper: the TEVs substrate landscapes, in which the varying sequence is the seven-residue substrate motif rather than the protease; and the in vitro and re-testing panels of Fig. 1e, 3a, 3b, 4d and 4e, each covering fewer than twenty distinct protease genotypes.

remark: The reference sequence is the library parent TEVp 0, the 242-residue NIa protease of UniProt P04517 carrying T17S, L56V, N68D, I77V, S135G and S219V; the paper states no sequence, so the parent residue at each scanned position was read off the site-saturation scan, where the parent's own row reads exactly 0 at all 234 positions, and the result was corroborated against 44 mutation labels printed in full elsewhere in the workbook, which verify without exception. Variants are named in the source by a three- or six-letter code over the randomized clusters, and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a cluster letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing. Libraries A (positions 30-32), B (217-219) and AB (both) are pooled, being the same measurement on the same parent in the same units; they share no variant with one another, so the pooling rests on that shared parent rather than on any overlapping measurement. Across all three libraries 241522 of 505580 protease-substrate combinations read NA, the pair never having been observed, and are dropped. protein: McbA, an ATP-dependent amide synthetase that couples a carboxylic acid and an amine
readout: Percent conversion to moclobemide, as a fold change against wild-type McbA
assay_method: Cell-free DNA assembly and cell-free gene expression of each McbA variant, followed by a functional assay reading percent conversion of the amine and acid substrates to the amide product by LC-MS, normalized to wild-type McbA measured on the same plate. Site-saturation hot-spot screen across 64 residues, n = 1 per variant.
remark: The reference sequence is the assayed construct, Strep-II- and TEV-tagged McbA translated from the supplementary DNA, and residue numbering follows that construct rather than the mature enzyme; after the 23-residue tag it is identical to UniProt R4R1U5 at 494 of 495 positions, the exception being the initiator methionine replaced by the glycine the TEV site leaves behind, and all 64 screened positions verify against it. The screen measures the parent once at every one of the 64 positions rather than defining it as 1, so the WT row is the mean of those 64 measurements, which themselves span 0.688 to 1.215 and are the clearest available statement of the assay's reproducibility at n = 1. Empty cells are dropped. Not extracted from this paper: the four-site combinatorial training and test libraries deposited on GitHub, which measure a different library on the same enzyme; the zero-shot prediction tables, which are computed rather than assayed; and the Fig. 2b substrate scope, which varies the reaction rather than the protein.

readout: Yield of the cis-2a cyclopropane product (percent)
assay_method: Whole-cell cyclopropanation of styrene with ethyl diazoacetate in 96-well plate format, product quantified by chromatography against an internal standard; five active-site residues (56, 57, 59, 60, 89) were randomized and variants identified by evSeq. Parent and 395 variants across an initial site-saturation set and two rounds of active-learning-selected combinations.
remark: The reference sequence is ParLQ translated from the supplementary DNA of Table S1, 199 residues including the C-terminal LE-His6 tag, and positions 56, 57, 59, 60 and 89 read WYLQF, matching the parent code the source data uses; no UniProt entry for ParPgb was found, so the sequence rests on the supplement alone. Variants are named in the source by a five-letter code over the randomized sites and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a code letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing; the parent's own code WYLQF becomes the WT row. The readout is the source's cis-2a yield column as it stands. Not extracted from this paper: the trans-2a yield on its own, which the source provides but which has no higher-is-better orientation, since the paper treats more trans product as worse rather than better; the plate-normalized ALDE objective, which is a restatement of the same pair of yields; and the public benchmark landscapes the paper runs simulations on, which belong to the publications that measured them.

protein: AtHMT, the Arabidopsis thaliana halide/thiocyanate methyltransferase HOL1
readout: Methyltransferase activity as a fold change against wild-type AtHMT
assay_method: Crude-lysate screening of individually constructed site-directed mutants in 96-well format, activity taken as the initial slope of the coupled methyltransfer assay and normalized to wild-type AtHMT on the same plate. Round 1 of the autonomous engineering campaign, two plates of 88 new mutants each, three or more replicate slopes per well.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q0WP12 unmodified, against which all 180 distinct mutations named in the primer plate maps verify at offset 0. There is no WT row: the readout is normalized to wild type on each plate, which is 1.0 by construction rather than by measurement, and the empty-vector control is not a variant; the positive control V140T is measured three times across the two plates, giving 1.78, 2.12 and 2.76, and its mean is used, that spread of 0.98 fold being the clearest indication of plate-to-plate reproducibility here. Variant identity is not in the screening file, whose rows are plate wells; it is recovered by joining each well to the primer plate map of Supplementary Data 1, where the mutation is encoded in the primer name. Not extracted from this paper: rounds 2 to 4 for this enzyme, which are built on several different improved parents per round with no per-well template assignment shipped, so a variant's full genotype cannot be reconstructed; and the whole YmPhytase campaign, for which no sequence is given in the paper and no reference accession could be found, so its 180 round-one mutants cannot be placed on any sequence.

protein: pCNF-RS, a Methanocaldococcus jannaschii tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase engineered to charge p-cyanophenylalanine
readout: Amber suppression activity as a fold change against wild-type pCNF-RS
assay_method: Fluorescence of a sfGFP amber-suppression reporter in E. coli, built and screened by an automated biofoundry in 96-well format, with fitness computed against the activity of wild-type pCNF-RS. Four rounds of 96 variants each: an ESM-2 zero-shot selection followed by three rounds chosen by a multilayer-perceptron fitness predictor retrained on the accumulated data.
remark: The reference sequence is pCNF-RS as given in the supplementary information, 306 residues, which differs from wild-type MjTyrRS (UniProt Q57834) at the six specificity positions Y32L, L65V, F108W, Q109M, D158G and I159A and reads HPMD at the four randomized positions 283 to 286, matching the code the source data uses for the wild type. Variants are named in the source by a four-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing. There is no WT row: the library did not sample the parent code HPMD, and the readout is defined against wild-type pCNF-RS, which is 1.0 by that definition rather than by measurement. Not extracted from this paper: the UBC9 and ubiquitin benchmark landscapes in Supplementary Data 1, which were measured by other publications and belong to them.

protein: SpCas9, the Streptococcus pyogenes CRISPR-associated endonuclease; variants alter six PAM-interacting residues of the PI domain
readout: log10 HT-PAMDA cleavage rate constant on the NAAA PAM
assay_method: High-throughput PAM determination assay (HT-PAMDA): each SpCas9 variant is incubated with a library of randomized-PAM substrates and cleavage is followed over time by sequencing, giving a first-order rate constant per PAM. Variants come from bacterial selections on a range of target PAMs and from random sampling of the SpCas9(6AA) library.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q99ZW2 unmodified, and residues 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337 read DSGERT, which is the code the source data itself uses for wild-type SpCas9. Enzymes are named in the source by a six-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the wild type, a letter equal to the wild-type residue contributing nothing; 16 codes were isolated independently two or three times across different bacterial selections and their measurements are averaged, agreeing to a median of 0.48 log10 units with a worst case of 3.85, which is the only reproducibility estimate the table offers. Supplementary Note 3 lists the six randomized positions as D1135, S1135, G1218, E1219, R1335 and T1337, naming 1135 twice; Supplementary Figure 7 gives 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337, and Q99ZW2 reads S at 1136, so the figure's numbering is followed. Not extracted from this paper: the PAMmla predictions of Supplementary Table 2 and the 64 million predicted enzyme profiles, which are computed rather than assayed; and the GUIDE-seq2 results of Supplementary Table 6, which measure off-target editing at genomic sites rather than a fitness per enzyme variant. The article itself is paywalled and is not redistributed in papers/; the supplementary tables it draws on are open and are staged instead.

assay_method: High-throughput PAM determination assay (HT-PAMDA): each SpCas9 variant is incubated with a library of randomized-PAM substrates and cleavage is followed over time by sequencing, giving a first-order rate constant per PAM. Variants come from bacterial selections on a range of target PAMs and from random sampling of the SpCas9(6AA) library.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q99ZW2 unmodified, and residues 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337 read DSGERT, which is the code the source data itself uses for wild-type SpCas9. Enzymes are named in the source by a six-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the wild type, a letter equal to the wild-type residue contributing nothing; 16 codes were isolated independently two or three times across different bacterial selections and their measurements are averaged, agreeing to a median of 0.48 log10 units with a worst case of 3.85, which is the only reproducibility estimate the table offers. Supplementary Note 3 lists the six randomized positions as D1135, S1135, G1218, E1219, R1335 and T1337, naming 1135 twice; Supplementary Figure 7 gives 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337, and Q99ZW2 reads S at 1136, so the figure's numbering is followed. Not extracted from this paper: the PAMmla predictions of Supplementary Table 2 and the 64 million predicted enzyme profiles, which are computed rather than assayed; and the GUIDE-seq2 results of Supplementary Table 6, which measure off-target editing at genomic sites rather than a fitness per enzyme variant. The article itself is paywalled and is not redistributed in papers/; the supplementary tables it draws on are open and are staged instead.
